title: Multiview capture shading modes (clay / curvature) so agents can read shallow sculpt features
user-messages: helper class? why helper class for an endpoint? that is stupid one class
description:
/ui/multiview grids come out dark navy on dark grey with very low contrast (see MESH-68's tmp/mesh68/round3.png in its worktree). A vision agent judging shape from them can barely see shallow ridges, valleys and creases. mesh.fs shades with a single Lambert term, max(dot(n, -lightDir), 0.2), times a dark solidColor, so most of the sphere sits in a narrow band of dark values.

Add a shading option for capture, e.g. `shading` on /ui/multiview with these values:
- `default`: today's look.
- `clay`: light grey albedo, key light plus fill, light background.
- `matcap`: a fixed studio matcap, the same in every view.
- `curvature` (or `cavity`): shading that darkens concave and brightens convex areas, so shallow sculpt features read.
- An optional per-view light that follows the camera (a headlight), so no view is lit from behind.

The viewer's normal look stays unchanged; only the capture switches shading and then restores it.
definition-of-done:
1. /ui/multiview (and ixdar-cli multiview) accept a shading parameter with at least default, clay and curvature.
2. The scene's shading and background are restored after capture.
3. Before/after multiview PNGs of the MESH-68 sculpted sphere (stroke_sculpt_sphere.dsl, or a plain sphere with a shallow bump if MESH-68 has not landed) are saved under tmp/. In clay and curvature, the nose crease and eye sockets read clearly in every view.
4. A measurement in tmp/<ticket>-measurements.json: the luminance standard deviation inside the mesh silhouette, default vs clay vs curvature.

5. The mesh viewer has a key or button that cycles default/clay/curvature and one that toggles the headlight. The current look shows in the scene's status line, and clay/curvature use the light palette.
6. POST /ui/shading (ixdar-cli shading) sets the viewer's look and leaves it on.
7. No CaptureShading helper class: the look lives on the scene (one setter that also swaps the palette), /ui/shading calls it, and /ui/multiview saves, sets and restores it inline.
testing-plan:
1. Load a sculpted sphere and capture multiview with shading=default, clay and curvature; compare the three PNGs.
2. Take a normal screenshot after each capture and check the viewer's look is unchanged.
3. Compute the luminance standard deviation inside the silhouette for each mode and record it in the measurements file.
changes-made: mesh.fs/mesh.vs: shadingStyle uniform (default/clay/curvature); curvature is screen-space mean curvature from view-space normal and position derivatives, scaled by mesh radius; clay/curvature lights follow the camera (key upper-left, or headlight)
SurfaceShading enum + HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.surfaceShading/headlight fields; AssimpModelRuntime resets the shared program to default

CaptureShading: parses shading/headlight, swaps runtime look and PAPER palette (light background) for the capture, restores in a finally; MultiviewScreenshot takes shading + headlight (ixdar-cli multiview --shading --headlight)
dsl/shallow_sculpt_sphere.dsl: sphere with a shallow nose ridge, eye sockets and equatorial crease for before/after captures

Superseded: CaptureShading deleted. The look lives on MeshNodeViewerScene (surfaceShading, headlight, setSurfaceLook swaps to PAPER for clay/curvature and back to the scene's palette for default; renderScene pushes it onto whatever runtime is installed, so it survives model reloads)
Keys in the mesh viewer: M cycles default -> clay -> curvature, H toggles the headlight; the STATE log line shows look=<MODE>[+headlight]

New POST /ui/shading (ixdar-cli shading [mode] [--headlight]) sets the look and leaves it on, or reports it with no args; /ui/multiview saves the scene's look, sets the requested one and restores it in finally, params documented in its own describe(); SurfaceShading.named parses the mode
review-summary: The mesh viewer gains clay and curvature surface looks with an optional headlight, toggled by keys, the /ui/shading route, or per multiview capture. Default captures are dark navy on dark grey, so a vision agent cannot see shallow ridges, creases and sockets.
